subject: Post-demo: model fit, evals & quality regression follow-up
messages:
From: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@acme-retail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Park <tpark@acme-retail.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up from demo — regression observed in latest model update

Thanks again for the walkthrough today, Marissa — appreciate the time. A quick recap from our side and the blocker we hit this morning: after we upgraded to the model version you recommended (redwood-model-v4.1), our product team saw a notable drop in quality for our returns categorization flows. We ran the same prompt set against v3.2 and v4.1 and the precision for "reason classification" dropped from 92% -> 73% on our sample.

I attached the sample prompts and a short CSV of the benchmark outputs (acme-benchmark-results.csv). The team flagged several examples where the newer model hallucinated product attributes. For trialing we need: 1) a quick analysis of the diff between v3.2 and v4.1, 2) options to pin or rollback while we investigate, and 3) recommended evaluation prompts or metric definitions we should add to the shared suite.

Can you let us know the earliest you can look at the diffs and propose next steps? We’d like to avoid a full rollback if a targeted pin/canary is possible.

Thanks — Sara
Sara Jenkins
Sr. Product Manager, Acme Retail
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T18:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — regression observed in latest model update

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear reproduction and the benchmark CSV. Really sorry you hit that. Quick recap and proposed next steps:  

- What I saw in your CSV: clear drop in precision on the returns "reason classification" slice when moving from redwood-model-v3.2 -> v4.1. Some hallucination cases in v4.1 on product attributes.
- Proposed next steps:
  1) Engineering (Rishi) will run a targeted diff analysis between the two model artifacts and share a short diff summary.
  2) We can pin your production route to redwood-model-v3.2 while we validate (no need for full infra rollback). Pinning is supported at the route-level and can be timeboxed.
  3) We'll add your sample prompts to a shared eval set and run a canary: 5% of traffic to v4.1 vs 95% pinned to v3.2 to measure live delta before wider rollout.

Attached: acme-sample-prompts.txt (your examples), and I’ll ask Rishi to attach the diff-summary once he runs the analysis. Also adding a link to a shared benchmark folder where we’ll publish the full runs: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDEf-acme-benchmarks

Next meeting? I propose a 30-min follow-up on Friday to go over the diff and the canary plan. Rishi/Neha — can you confirm availability and ETA on the diff?

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — regression observed in latest model update

Hi all — dug into the artifacts this morning. Summary (high level):

- Root cause hypothesis: v4.1 includes an updated tokenization preprocessing step and a slightly different prompting initialization that increases descriptive completion but reduces conservative entity anchoring for short, tabular-like prompts (your returns prompts fall into that category).
- Diff summary attached: diff-summary.txt (includes layer/weight table checksums + a short notes section). Notable change: attention layer bias in encoder block 6 altered during finetune stage.

Options:
1) Pin route to redwood-model-v3.2 (route-level pin) — instant, reversible.
2) Canary: start at 5% traffic to v4.1 with the rest pinned to v3.2, collect your key metrics (precision, recall, false-positive rate on reason classification) for 48–72 hours.
3) If you prefer a rollback, we can do a controlled rollback to v3.2 across the environment, but that’s heavier and impacts any improvements in other slices.

How to pin (internal command):
- redwood route update --route acme-returns --model redwood-model-v3.2 --pin true --reason "regression observed 2026-12-01"

ETA: I can produce the full diff report + suggested prompt augmentation in ~24 hours. Will attach diff-summary.txt now with the checksums and a short checklist for verification.

-Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Staff ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@acme-retail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Park <tpark@acme-retail.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-03T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — regression observed in latest model update

Thanks Rishi — that explanation lines up with what our ML team suspected. Two quick asks before we lock to a plan:

1) Timeline — if you can get the full diff report and suggested prompt augmentations in 24 hours we’ll plan the canary for Friday.
2) Metrics — we’ll track precision and semantic accuracy (we typically compute an F1 on the labeled returns set). Please include instructions for how you’ll surface those in the Redwood Console (per-route dashboard or shared CSV).

Quoted for context:
> On Tue, Dec 1, 2026 at 6:03 PM, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> > Attached: acme-sample-prompts.txt (your examples), and I’ll ask Rishi to attach the diff-summary once he runs the analysis. Also adding a link to a shared benchmark folder where we’ll publish the full runs: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDEf-acme-benchmarks

We’re happy to do a 30-min session Friday. Can you confirm availability and the HubSpot record so our procurement team can align on any temporary pin SLA changes?

— Sara
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — regression observed in latest model update

Thanks — confirmed on next steps and timing. Action items: 

- Rishi: deliver full diff report + prompt augmentation suggestions by 2026-12-03T18:00-08:00 (attached diff-summary.txt).
- Marissa/Neha: create the canary plan (5% to v4.1 vs 95% pinned to v3.2) and publish the run to the shared Drive folder. I’ll configure the per-route dashboard to surface precision/F1 and share a CSV export.
- Laura: I’ll loop you in on procurement/getting a signed mutual action plan for the temporary pin (MAP-Acme.docx).

Meeting: Friday 2026-12-05 11:00 PT — I sent a calendar invite. HubSpot record for the deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/ACME-2026-07.

If the canary shows improvement in the targeted slices we’ll expand; if it shows sustained regression we’ll keep the pin and open a deeper investigation (possible retrain on the anchored prompts).

Thanks everyone — feel free to add anything I missed.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
